overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated YouTube Shorts data reveals that extreme cosmic anomalies and 'What If' hypothetical scenarios involving planets and space (e.g., liquid diamond planets, dark planets, extreme rain phenomena) drive the highest velocity, views-per-day, and engagement (likes-per-view). Content published within the last 7 days heavily outperforms older archive pieces, indicating strong algorithm favorability for high-concept space curiosities with visual thought-experiment hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) garnered over 1,000 and 970 views rapidly with strong like ratios (up to 38 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical planetary physics and extreme survival thought experiments in space.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring impossible planetary conditions like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) consistently hit near or above 1,000 views within short timeframes.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form spotlights on bizarre exoplanets with extreme physical properties.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on psychological or brain hacks like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A) and 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (ef3ND4qiRHc) yielded very low views and minimal likes compared to cosmic content.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological trivia shorts unless paired with a high-stakes visual mystery hook.

weak_patterns.pattern: Standard Biological Facts Without a Twist
weak_patterns.evidence: Simple animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (AXAfwrzzEdU) plateaued at lower view counts and zero comments, lacking the curiosity gap of space or mystery content.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid straightforward biological listicles; pivot animal content strictly toward cinematic survival or bizarre evolutionary anomalies.

next_video.hook_style: What If / Extreme Physics Curiosity Gap
next_video.concept: What happens if you fall into the coldest known place in the universe—the Boomerang Nebula?
next_video.opening_direction: Start inside a total vacuum where absolute zero instantly freezes matter faster than liquid nitrogen.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that this cosmic freezer is actually colder than the background radiation of the universe itself, absorbing heat from empty space.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high performance of 'What If' space scenarios and extreme temperature/environment hooks like the star colder than ice and burning ice planets.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must focus on the Boomerang Nebula, not previously covered planets or stars.

experiment: Test a 20-second 'What If' space scenario featuring an entirely unexplored cosmic phenomenon against our standard exoplanet spotlight to check if hypothetical immersion outperforms descriptive facts.
